Phase 1 — UX Audit

Friction Log

12 usability issues identified across the homepage, each mapped to the UX principle it violates and the impact it has on a first-time visitor.

#IssueWhy It's a ProblemUX Principle ViolatedImpact on User
1Impact stats show "0+ Members, 0+ Events, 0+ Collaborations, 0"Numbers display as zero/blank, killing the credibility moment meant to build trustAesthetic-Usability / Trust signal failure — broken data reads as an inactive orgNew visitors assume no real activity and bounce before About/Activities
2FAQ accordion — only the first question shows an answer; the other two show nothingUsers click expecting an answer and get nothing — a dead interactionVisibility of system status (Nielsen #1)Frustration, loss of trust in rest of site's functionality
3Timeline numbered 1→6 but runs in reverse chronological order (2024→2018), item "6" emptyNumbering implies forward progression but the story reads backwards, ending on a dangling empty itemMatch between system & real world / ConsistencyConfusing origin story — can't follow how the community grew
4Hero has two competing CTAs: unbranded bit.ly "Join" link + a Contact icon button beside itBit.ly gives no preview of destination (untrustworthy); two CTAs of near-equal weight competeVisual hierarchy / Recognition over recallUsers hesitate to click an unbranded link; primary action unclear
5Three hero images (team photos) stacked with no captions, alt text, or narrative link to headlineImages take up hero real estate but communicate nothing — "AI community" claim isn't shownAesthetic-Usability + Content as design materialFirst-screen impression feels generic/stock
6Working Groups (Individual/Industry/Academia) each just say "Join" linking to bare Airtable formsUsers asked to fill a form before understanding what they're signing up forRecognition rather than recall / Informed consentLow conversion — won't submit a form to an unknown commitment
7Sponsor & Collaboration logos shown with zero labels/links (including a tiny illegible base64 icon)Visitors can't identify partner organizations, undermining credibilityRecognition over recall / Accessibility (no alt text)Social proof section provides zero actual proof
8Nav mixes same-page anchors (#about, #faq) with external links (Team, Blogs→Medium) with no visual distinctionUsers can't predict if a click scrolls or navigates awayConsistency and standardsDisorientation, especially on mobile
9Chapters section lists 5 cities as a plain numbered list with only 2 generic photosHyperlocal value proposition isn't actually delivered locallyMatch between system & real worldA user in Madurai/Trichy has no path to their local chapter
10Footer repeats nav links + "Documentation/Press Files" with no visible destinations, duplicates contact infoRedundant content increases scan time without adding valueAesthetic-Usability / Minimalist design (Nielsen #8)Footer feels like boilerplate, reduces professionalism
11Heavy mixing of Tamil headings with English body copy, no language toggle, inconsistent script useSome users can't parse the headline; inconsistency feels unplannedAccessibility / ConsistencyReduces reach for the "anyone in Tamil Nadu" mission
12Single long-scroll page with 10+ sections, no progress indicator or sticky navHigh cognitive load; users lose track of where they areVisibility of system status / Flexibility & efficiencyDrop-off before reaching Contact/Join sections
Phase 2 — User Understanding

Who is this for, and why?

Target Users

  • Students & early-career learners in Tier-2/3 Tamil Nadu towns (Salem, Madurai, Trichy) — often first-generation tech learners with limited English fluency
  • College students & recent grads in Coimbatore/Chennai seeking community, mentorship, portfolio-building
  • Industry professionals & academics exploring collaboration, sponsorship, or speaking opportunities
  • Existing members checking events, chapter info, or resources

User Goals

  • Quickly understand: "What is this, is it legit, is it for someone like me?"
  • Find their nearest chapter and how to get involved locally
  • Join with minimal friction — one clear primary action
  • Access learning resources without digging
  • Partners: understand collaboration paths

Business Goal of the Website

Convert visitors into registered community members and chapter participants, while building enough credibility (visible activity, real numbers, labeled partner logos) to attract sponsors, academic partners, and volunteer mentors — growing AI Tamil Nadu's reach across all of Tamil Nadu, not just Coimbatore.

Phase 3 & 4 — Redesign & Explanation

Top issues addressed

Of the 12 friction points, issues #1, #3, #4/#5, #8, #9, #12 were prioritized for the homepage redesign — chosen because they sit directly on the path to the site's core conversion action: joining a chapter.

1 Hero Section

Problem
Competing CTAs, decorative-only images, bilingual clarity, no immediate proof of activity.
Solution
Single primary CTA ("Find Your Chapter"), secondary text-link for contact, restructured bilingual headline with English sub-line, and a live stat strip replacing broken "0+" counters with real numbers.
Why it works
One dominant action reduces decision fatigue (Hick's Law); the stat strip front-loads credibility exactly where eyes land first (Gutenberg diagram).
Expected outcome
Higher click-through on "Join," lower bounce rate, clearer first impression of an active organization.

2 Chapters Section — Interactive Map

Problem
Hyperlocal promise isn't locally actionable; flat list with no per-chapter path.
Solution
Interactive Tamil Nadu map with 5 pinned chapters (Coimbatore, Salem, Trichy, Chennai, Madurai). Clicking a pin opens a card with chapter story, focus areas, and a "Join [City] Chapter" button that pre-fills the registration form's location field.
Why it works
Spatial recognition (map) matches the mental model of "where is my nearest chapter" instantly — recognition over recall.
Expected outcome
Higher-quality sign-ups matched to the correct local chapter from day one, reinforcing the "hyperlocal" brand promise.

3 Sticky Navigation + Link Distinction

Problem
12-section long scroll with no orientation; nav doesn't distinguish in-page vs external links.
Solution
Sticky nav with scrollspy (active section highlighted). External links (Team, Blogs) get a small "↗" icon.
Why it works
Visibility of system status — users always know where they are and what a click will do.
Expected outcome
Reduced disorientation, more users reach Working Groups/Contact sections.

4 Timeline — Fixed Direction

Problem
Reverse-chronological numbering, dangling empty "6."
Solution
Re-sequenced 01–05, chronological 2018 → 2024, each with a one-line "what changed" description.
Why it works
Matches the real-world mental model — origin story now reads forward; removes the orphaned empty state.
Expected outcome
Clearer narrative of growth, builds trust through visible momentum.

5 Working Groups & FAQ

Problem
"Join" with no context; broken FAQ answers.
Solution
Each Working Group card gets "Who it's for" + "What you'll do" before the CTA. FAQ rebuilt as a fully working accordion (all 5 Q&As + 2 new FAQs: "Is it really free?", "Do I need coding experience?").
Why it works
Reduces perceived risk before a commitment; answers the exact anxieties of first-time AI learners.
Expected outcome
Higher Working Group conversion, fewer repetitive DMs/emails asking basic questions.

Summary

The throughline

The current site has the content needed (mission, chapters, activities, resources) but buries it in an undifferentiated long scroll with several broken/empty states (stats, FAQ, timeline) that quietly damage trust on a site whose entire value proposition is "join a real, active community."

The redesign's throughline is to make the hyperlocal promise spatially real (map-based chapters), fix every broken trust signal, and collapse two competing CTAs into one clear path to membership.

"From a long scroll of broken counters, dead FAQs, and a reverse timeline — to a trust-first, map-led homepage where every Tamil Nadu district has a working door in."
